# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 exporting manufacturers). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| supplier_diversity | Number of distinct input suppliers (standardized), 2021-2022 |
| export_growth_2023 | Export value growth in 2023 (percent index) |
| log_sales_2020 | Log sales, 2020 |
| years_exporting_2020 | Years since first export, standardized, 2020 |
| export_growth_2020 | Export value growth in 2020, standardized |
| buyer_rating_2023 | Average rating from foreign buyers, 2023 |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| product_group | Sector: durables / nondurables |
| inventory_days_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| foreign_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| share_imported_inputs_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| port_distance_km | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| certified_iso | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| debt_ratio_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Supplier diversification and export growth

**Conclusion: positive effect.** Preferred estimate: +0.69 percentage-index points of 2023 export growth per 1 SD increase in supplier diversity (HC1 SE 0.240, p = 0.0038, n = 2000). This is an association adjusted for pre-period covariates. It reads as causal only if those covariates capture all confounding.

## Specifications estimated (4 in total, OLS, HC1 robust SEs)
| # | Specification | Coef | SE | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Raw: growth2023 ~ diversity | 2.553 | 0.246 | 3e-25 |
| 2 | + log_sales_2020, years_exporting_2020, export_growth_2020 | 0.691 | 0.240 | 0.0040 |
| 3 (preferred) | + all the other 2020 pre-period controls (region, listed, product group, inventory days, foreign-owned, import share, port distance, ISO, debt ratio) | 0.693 | 0.240 | 0.0038 |
| 4 | Spec 3 + buyer_rating_2023 | -2.121 | 0.233 | 8e-20 |

## Notes
- The raw estimate (2.55) is inflated by confounding. Controlling for firm size and the other pre-period characteristics cuts it by about 73%. Specs 2 and 3 agree closely.
- I did not prefer spec 4. `buyer_rating_2023` is measured after the treatment (2021-22 diversity) and is itself strongly driven by diversity (coefficient 0.66, t = 23). It is a post-treatment variable, so it may be a mediator or a collider. Conditioning on it flips the sign to -2.12, and I attribute that to the conditioning, not to a real negative effect. I report the spec for transparency only.
- Spec 3 includes only variables measured in 2020 or earlier, before the treatment window, so it avoids that problem. Unobserved confounding remains possible. I did not run nonlinearity, heterogeneity, or instrument checks.
- The PI hoped for a positive result. The positive result in spec 3 comes from the pre-specified, covariate-adjusted model, not from a search over specifications. The effect is much smaller than the raw association suggests.

content.text:
I approved the report and wrote `verdict.json`.

I re-ran the analyst's four specifications. The preferred estimate matches: about +0.69 index points of 2023 export growth per 1 SD of supplier diversity (HC1 SE 0.24, p = 0.004, n = 2000).

I also tried three extra checks of my own, and the estimate held up in each:
- **Quadratic term:** adding the square of supplier diversity gave 0.69, and the squared term was null (p = 0.93).
- **Nonlinear controls:** adding squares and an interaction of the size and prior-growth controls left the estimate at 0.69.
- **Interactions:** letting the effect vary by product group and region left the main coefficient positive but less precise (0.85, p = 0.09). None of the interaction terms was significant.

The report also handles the main pitfalls well. It leaves buyer rating out of the preferred model because it is measured after the treatment, and it explains why including it flips the sign. It lists all four specifications and describes the result as an adjusted association rather than a proven cause. It does say unobserved confounding is still possible.

The one real limit is that the controls only cover observed pre-period differences, which the report itself states.
